utterances.text: From the place in front of the local commune building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And who was there with you at that site where you were exchanged? Were there any people that used to work with you there as well?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: There was Veljo there. And then as we were departing, I saw Miroslav Tadic, called Brka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And at the site of the exchange itself, at the separation line with Gradacac, who was present there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: There were Veljo, then Tadic, then some soldiers were there. They negotiated about something. I don't know about what. So all of this was going on. And then on one side there was the International Red Cross. I don't know what they talked about. We were simply waiting to be exchanged. And this is how this exchange was conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicakcic, please tell us, at the time at this site, did they ask you whether you wanted to cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and I said that I wanted to cross over. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, in front of whom did you say that you wanted to cross over? Were there representatives of Gradacac there as well?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were representatives from the other side as well, and I think that there were some people from the Red Cross there too. I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the Red Cross, do you mean the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the international one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when you say "Veljo," which Veljo do you have in mind? Please give us the last name. Was it Maslic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Maslic. He was involved in the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicakcic, did you reunite with your family then?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about your job? Did somebody get hired instead of you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Where do you mean; in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: You mean when I left?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: My brother had a work obligation, and then I asked them, since he was an elderly person, I asked them whether he could substitute me there. And we knew the director and he had some influence, and therefore, my brother remained with the fire brigade upon my departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicakcic, did you have any other brothers in Samac in 1992 in addition to this brother who got your job?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I had two other brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did they remain in Samac during the war?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have their families?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did their families remain in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicakcic, while you were in Gradacac, did somebody enter your apartment or your house?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who remained to live in the house where you used to live?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: My parents, father and mother, and my eldest brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicakcic, did you return to Samac?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please tell us, Mr. Bicakcic, where are you employed now?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: In the same unit where I used to work before the war. I submitted a request upon my return to Samac, a request to the municipal assembly, and then they replied to the director saying that, "If he is needed, then hire him." Therefore, the director gave me the same job I had before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bicakcic. I have no further questions. PRESIDING OFFICER: Cross-examination for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we just be given a minute to switch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bicakcic. My name is Phillip Weiner. I'm a Prosecutor with the ICTY, and I'm going to ask you some questions. Sir, you testified that you were a member of the fire brigade in -- prior to April 16th and after, and that after April 16th it was still multi-ethnic. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, isn't it a fact that after May of 1992, which was the first of those two sheets that you looked at, certain non-Serbs in the fire department started leaving?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Not Serbs? No one was forced out of the fire brigade. No one was dismissed from the fire brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...was, sir. Sir --

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: It was up to his own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question was: Were people, non-Serbs, leaving? I didn't -- that's my question. Yes or no. I can give you names, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: From the fire brigade, you mean? No, they didn't leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you look at 81A, in May we see the name Marko Nodjic [phoen] and Fuad Kuburic [phoen]. You don't see their names on June or July, do you, sir? It's in the records. Were Marko Nodjic, Fuad Kuburic on the fire brigade in June of 1992? 81B, please. You'll see their names do not appear.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: This Kuburic Fuad, he fled of his own accord. He just disappeared. He abandoned the service. He didn't report to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: People were leaving. That's all I'm saying is people were leaving. And in June, Mirsad Hecimovic, he also left after June; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Mirsad Hecimovic, he was taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He was no longer on the fire brigade after June? Just -- that's all -- whatever reason, he wasn't on the fire brigade after June. Do you know what the reason was for him being taken into custody?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That's up to the person who arrested him. He probably knows, and he must know why he was taken into custody. So I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact a year later in June or July of 1993 a whole group of non-Serb firemen left? Sefik Pistoljevic [phoen], Salkan Pistoljevic [phoen], Isudin Ibralic, Suad, Sulejmanovic. They all left too?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they left, just as I had left because I wanted to. And they wanted to go too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you also aware -- or let me ask you this question, sir: I know some of these non-Serbs were sent to Brvnik [phoen] to dig trenches. Were you one of those persons that had to dig trenches at Brvnik at the front lines in June 1993? People such as Sefik Pistoljevic had to go to the front lines and dig trenches while he was a fireman for five days. Were you one of those non-Serb firemen that had to do that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: We did go for a couple of days, but it wasn't often. When we were free, when we were not on duty, when our shift was not on duty. And then we'd again return to our same workplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You've indicated you have some brothers. Now, Mehmed, is it your brother who was a fireman, Mehmed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And Mirsad -- Mirsad the butcher, same last name as yours, is he related to you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how is he related to you; a cousin, an uncle?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: They are my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mirsad, was he a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was he Mirsad the butcher who got into an incident with Nassir Izetbegovic [phoen]? Was he involved in an incident, that Mirsad the butcher? Tota. Tota. You know Tota -- I'm sorry, not Tota. Tota Ramusovic. Do you know Tota Ramusovic, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was your brother Mirsad the butcher the one that was involved in an incident with Tota Ramusovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. My brother is not a butcher. He's not a butcher. I mean, that's wrong if you have such information. He's not a butcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There's a Mirsad who's known as Mirsad the butcher. Is that your brother? That's a nickname -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No, no. "The butcher" is not his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let us move on. You were aware at the time that you were working in Samac, you and your brothers, that a number of non-Serbs were being detained; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And these included the leaders of the SDA political party Sulejman Tihic, Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as you travelled throughout the municipality as part of the fire department, you were aware that a large number of Muslims and Croats were being detained at various locations in Bosanski Samac; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And they were being detained at the SUP, the police station or SUP?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Territorial Defence building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At the high school and primary school, or if you want to call it the secondary school and the primary school too?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were aware that people were being detained at Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, were you also detained -- were you also aware that these people who were being detained were being treated very poorly?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I can't say that. I wasn't there. I heard, but I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of very poor treatment, beatings, torture, murders that were occurring at these places of detention? Have you heard?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I heard, but I only heard about such things, but I didn't see whether anyone was beating anyone else or what they were doing as I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, are you aware that your own police chief and also the president of the -- your own police chief has pled guilty to persecution of the non-Serb prisoners, including beatings, murders, and torture? Were you aware of that, that Stevan Todorovic pled guilty to that? The police chief in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I heard something to that effect. I didn't really pay much attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that your city managers, as we would call it in the western part of the -- in the Western countries, the president of the executive or the executive board, Milan Simic, pled guilty to torturing a number of civilians who were detained in Bosanski Samac? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you -- on the other hand, you were never beaten or harmed. Is that true, sir? You were never arrested, never beaten, never harmed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your brothers, were they ever beaten or harmed or arrested?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No. As far as my brothers are concerned, they didn't get involved in politics. They weren't in any parties or anything, so nothing happened to them. We're simply not interested in politics and, therefore, it's no wonder that that is how we fared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were very lucky. You and your brothers are very lucky, because the other people, the other civilians, were severely beaten. Were you aware that the Crisis Staff, in May of 1992, issued an order to isolate members of the Croat community, where they were sent to the high school in Zasavica. Were you aware of a large number of Croats being sent to Zasavica and to the high school?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: You see, I don't know where people were detained or who was detained. I heard that there were camps, but I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this method of questioning. First of all, the Prosecutor asked three questions in one. "Had you heard of the order on the detention of Croats in Samac?" Then, "Were you aware that they were detained and taken into isolation?" And thirdly, what those places were. So could the witness be asked one question at a time, because he doesn't know which to answer. That's just my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The witness doesn't seem to have any problem answering.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that civilians were taken to Zasavica and held there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that the phrase used or the term used for their being held was "isolation"? Had you heard that used in reference to people being detained or do you recall back ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I heard it. I just heard it. But I don't know how one could --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I don't know if you're -- are you aware that Simo -- both Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic gave statements to the Office of the Prosecutor? If you're aware.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric indicated that the Crisis Staff issued an order to isolate the Croats in 1992 and they were sent to Zasavica. Does that refresh your recollection as to what happened?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you something quite frankly and openly. I know that people were held in detention, but if I had -- as if I had monitored anyone, who gave what orders, I had no idea. I just did my job honestly and decently as a fireman who was devoted to protection of the civilians. Everything else is simply what I heard. I don't know these things. I don't know who gave what orders and who detained people. So therefore, I can't answer these questions for you as if I had been in the Crisis Staff. I just heard about these things, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move on to two other -- a few other subjects, and we'll finish up for the day. With regard to your exchange, you were notified by a courier that you were to be exchanged; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said that the courier was a Muslim man; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he was a courier in 1993 in Samac, and his previous job was bank director; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Before the war, yes. Let's make it quite clear. Before the war, he was bank director, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So he went from bank director to courier during the war?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: That was his work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So he was at one point the bank director of which bank?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: The bank of Vinkovci. Of a Croatian bank. It was called the Vinkovci bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And then he became a courier where he was delivering messages, like to you that you were going to be exchanged. Now -- is that a yes or no or -- you nodded your head.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: For the record, you have to say yes or no because the transcript has to pick up the other language. Now, you would ask to leave in May. You wanted to leave Samac in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes. In May I put my name down for the exchange, and the exchange itself, the first exchange, was in May, and the second one was in December. There were only two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're also aware that other Muslims and Croats were trying to leave, escape, or get out? Isn't that true? Other Bosniaks, Muslims, Croats, however you want to describe it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you see, no one was forcing anyone to stay or to leave. It was up to each individual to put his name down for the exchange. That's what I did. Nobody forced me to be exchanged. I didn't have to. I could have easily stayed on doing my job, only I was separated from my family, and I'd had enough of being alone, and I wanted to reunite with my family after a year and a half. After all, it's a long time. It doesn't really matter where I was going to go. Gradacac is somewhere else. I just wanted to be with my family and my family with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're aware that some people were taking actions to leave. Had you heard that some people were offering bribes to be exchanged? Just whether or not you've heard it. Have you heard that people were taking -- were offering bribes to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: As far as bribes are concerned, I don't know anything about that. Nobody asked for any -- me for any money when I went. I don't know about others, whether there were any bribes or not. I just can't say whether someone -- anyone gave anything to anyone. All I know is that I didn't give anyone anything. No one asked me for a penny for the exchange. Nobody asked me for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you don't know what other people did, though. You don't know what other people and their families were doing either. No?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that people were paying to have false papers made so they could leave by way of Serbia? Were you aware of that, that papers were being falsified, identifications?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I heard of it. Again I wasn't present to be able to testify, to be a witness of that. I just heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were also aware that some people escaped by swimming across the Sava or sneaking out in whatever way they could?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: There were some such cases, but that was up to them. That was their affair. You should ask them about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were living alone, did any refugees ever move into your house?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: After you left in December of 1993, did anyone ever move into your home; refugees or persons unknown to you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No one moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that includes anyone you know? No one without permission moved into your home; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No, nobody except my parents. My parents were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you never lost any property. You never faced any eviction. Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No. No. I was not. As for other cases, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your brothers, did they lose any of their property or were they evicted from their homes?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: One brother was with me in the same yard. We had a little house. So he wasn't evicted either. And another brother, he has a couple of small rooms. It wasn't a real house. And another brother lived in a rented apartment. He didn't have anything of his own. He didn't have an apartment of his own. He was paying rent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So no one lost any of their property, including your brother who was renting. He wasn't forced out. Everyone maintained their property or their flats?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: These two brothers and myself, we were all living next to one another, really, in the same sort of yard. And this other one who was renting rooms, it was in a house owned by someone else, someone else's property.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, just one last area of questions. You indicated that you went to the front lines in Brvnik. Mr. Pistoljevic said he was there for five days. You were there for a couple of days. You did that on your spare time, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours. The witness is being referred to a statement of another witness, which is not allowed, according to the Rules of the Tribunal, and could the question be rephrased and the record corrected accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We've already covered this area before. I just want to clear up a couple issues in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you indicated that you -- PRESIDING OFFICER: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. PRESIDING OFFICER: You have one minute left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that you went to the front lines and you dug trenches. How many days -- you said you were out there for a couple days.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I was there for a couple of days. We agreed amongst ourselves, those of us who were there, who would go. I said, "I'll go." Nobody ordered people by name to go. There was no list of people who had to go. But we, amongst ourselves, agreed we need to help in digging the trenches. So several of us went and did that part of job, and then we returned to our regular jobs after those couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was there any fighting? Was any fighting going on there while you were digging the trenches?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: No. They wouldn't let us dig when there was firing. They wouldn't let us, but only when there was no shooting, no fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Again, we'll leave it at this last part of it. So there was no firing on, and you did that voluntarily, not as part of your work obligation? That was work that you volunteered to do, you personally, you and some of the others?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Those of us working in the fire brigade unit, we agreed amongst ourselves who would go. "I'll go for two. You'll go for two." It didn't matter. And then we came back to our workplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you did that voluntarily, not as part of any work obligation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: You see, I -- I don't know really how to call it. I don't know who provided this document saying that some people needed to go. I don't know these things. I just know that we were supposed to do it. Now, why it was that I went and not someone else, somebody had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we -- not Your Honour. Madam -- I was going to say Madam Director. We have approximately seven minutes banked from this morning. The first witness -- from the first witness we had four minutes, from the second witness we had three to four minutes. So we have an additional seven minutes in our bank. If you've kept your time -- if you've kept the time, you'll notice that we have a little bit more. PRESIDING OFFICER: So how many more minutes do you need? Two? You're sure?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I just want to finish this and then we can leave, because I -- and then redirect. PRESIDING OFFICER: Yes, redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just want to leave you with this question: While you were out there, the time that you were out there and the other firemen were out there, at any time was there any firing that was occurring? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: While we were at the trenches?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Or in the fire brigade? At the trenches?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At the trenches. Was there any firing occurring while you were out there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Even if fire was opened, we would take shelter. If somebody should open fire by chance, then we would take shelter until it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. My question is: Do you recall any firing occurring while you were out there back in 1993? Was it -- was there firing going on while you were out digging?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In Brvnik, digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: While I was digging the trench, or we were digging the trench, there was no firing. I am repeating. And should somebody fire a bullet or from a sniper, we would take shelter. And when this calms down, we'd go out again and finish what we had to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment for consultations, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: PRESIDING OFFICER: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicakcic, I have a couple of questions, so please put your headset on. The Prosecutor asked you about different ways of leaving Samac, and he asked you whether you had heard that there were false papers being made for money, and you answered that you had heard of such things, that this service was -- had to be paid for. Now, my question is, since the Prosecutor asked you, whether you had heard, you personally.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I just heard about it. I wasn't present to see anyone giving anyone any money for something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear, but I have another question. The Prosecutor also asked you whether you had offered anyone money for you to be exchanged. Now I'm going to ask you quite clearly. Did you hear that it was necessary --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir. Counsel, I didn't ask him if he offered anyone. He indicated that he hadn't offered anyone. I asked him if he was aware of any of the rumours that bribes were being paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So had you heard of rumours of bribes being needed for people to be exchanged? It's very simple. If you had, yes. If you hadn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM BICAKCIC
utterances.text: I can't explain now whether I had heard it or not. People say all kinds of things. I wasn't present. I don't know whether anyone gave anyone such money. As to whether I heard it, there were rumours, but I paid no attention. There are people who just talk, gossip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bicakcic. I have no further questions. PRESIDING OFFICER: Thank you for coming today. You may go now.
